conversation:
Counselor: Hi, thanks for coming in today. How are you feeling about your smoking?

Patient: Honestly, I've been thinking about it a lot lately. My doctor told me last month that my lungs are showing early signs of damage. That scared me.

Counselor: That sounds like it was a real wake-up call. Have you thought about quitting before?

Patient: Oh yeah, I've tried a few times. Last year I used the nicotine patch for about six weeks — that was my longest stretch. Before that I tried just stopping cold turkey but that only lasted maybe two or three days.

Counselor: Six weeks is actually a meaningful attempt. What happened at the end of those six weeks?

Patient: Work stress. It was a brutal project and I just cracked one night.

Counselor: So stress is a big trigger for you?

Patient: Definitely. And mornings — I have a cigarette with my coffee every single morning.

Counselor: What worries you most about quitting this time?

Patient: The stress thing. I don't know what I'd do when things get hard at work. Also I'm worried about weight gain.

Counselor: I recommend varenicline, a stress-management plan, and a nutritionist referral. Does a quit date in the next two weeks feel doable?

Patient: Maybe. I'd like to set a date. I think I'm ready to try this time.

Counselor: Let's schedule you for varenicline and set that date today.

Counselor: What brings you in today?

Patient: My wife made me come. I don't really think I need to quit. I've smoked for twenty years, I feel fine.

Counselor: Have you ever thought about quitting?

Patient: Not really. Maybe when I'm older. Right now it helps me relax after work.

Counselor: Are there any health concerns you've noticed?

Patient: A bit of a cough in the mornings but nothing major. Look, I'm not here to be lectured. I just want to keep the wife happy.

Counselor: I understand. I'm not here to pressure you. Can I share some information about what's available if you ever do decide to try?

Patient: Sure, whatever.

Counselor: There are medications and support programs that make quitting much easier than going cold turkey. When you're ready, we're here. No pressure today.

Patient: Alright. I'll think about it. Maybe.
